meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to mean'.

examples.trans: Pasha, what does all this mean?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'how; as', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'well; come on', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'he; it', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'oneself, myself, himself', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я и сама хорошо проведу время.
examples.trans: I'll have a good time on my own.

examples.text: Николай Филиппович, простите меня, пожалуйста. Я сам не знаю, как это произошло.
examples.trans: Nikolai Filippovich, please forgive me. I don't know myself how it happened.

examples.text: Я сам не знаю, как это произошло.
examples.trans: I don't know myself how it happened.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to do, to make', paired with 'сделать'.

examples.trans: Hi, Arkady Borisovich. What are you doing?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.
And does the governor support you?

examples.text: Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'бовать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to try; to taste', paired with 'попробовать'.

examples.text: Слушай, Аркаша, а ты не пробовал это вложить?
examples.trans: Listen, Arkasha, have you ever tried investing it?

говорить.gloss: to speak, to say, to talk

meanings.en: to speak, to say, to talk
meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to speak, to say, to talk', paired with 'сказать'.
High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'no; there isn't', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?
And this is for you. A toy car!

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'пробовать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to try', paired with 'пробовать'.

examples.text: Как я могу это забыть? Ну, давай попробуем.
examples.trans: How can I forget that? Well, let's try.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'казать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to say, to tell', paired with 'говорить'.

examples.trans: Tell us, when will your programme be out?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'if', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'нравиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to be liked, to please', paired with 'нравиться'.

examples.trans: Don't be afraid, you'll like it.

examples.text: А придётся! Не бойся, тебе понравится.
examples.trans: Well, you'll have to! Don't be afraid, you'll like it.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, that; it is', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'masterpiece' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: A masterpiece was made out of nothing.
This soup is a real masterpiece.
Well done. Practically a masterpiece out of nothing.

приготовить.gloss: to prepare, to cook, to make

meanings.en: to prepare, to cook, to make
meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'готовить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to prepare, to cook, to make', paired with 'готовить'.

examples.text: Я торт приготовила. Ты любишь сладкое?
examples.trans: I made a cake. Do you have a sweet tooth?

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('other, another, different').

examples.text: Послушайте, а можно в другое место? Здесь плохо пахнет.
examples.trans: Listen, could we go somewhere else? It smells bad in here.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'hello'.

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'щаться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to communicate, to talk with'.

examples.trans: I am not allowed to talk with you.

examples.text: Мне с вами вообще общаться нельзя. Всего доброго.
examples.trans: I'm not allowed to talk to you at all. Good day.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'with', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'видимый'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('invisible').

examples.trans: The universe is wrapped in thin invisible threads.

examples.text: Шеф говорит, что это очень невидимый выбор.
examples.trans: The chef says that this is a very invisible choice.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'friend' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: This is Vanya, my childhood friend.

examples.text: Это Паша, мой заместитель. Это Ваня, друг моего детства.
examples.trans: This is Pasha, my deputy. This is Vanya, my childhood friend.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and, but; so', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'romance, romantic atmosphere' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: There is no romance in it at all!

examples.trans: By the way, they called from the Italian restaurant. They're giving Dad a romantic dinner for two.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'for; behind', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'my, mine', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'толик'). Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'small table, café table' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Они заняли свободный столик у окна.
examples.trans: They took a free table near the window.
Would you like to sit at an available table?
To a guest at the next table.

meanings.note: Prefix 'из-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'винить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to excuse; (imperative) sorry, excuse me', paired with 'извинять'.

examples.trans: Thank you, Marina. Sorry, I'm in a hurry.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'верное').

examples.trans: Well, probably somewhere in the archive.
He has probably already come home.

examples.text: Наверное, что-то серьёзное у вас. Девочка уже две недели лежит в областной клинике!
examples.trans: It must be something serious for you. The girl has been lying in the regional clinic for two weeks already!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'over, above; at', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: The lamp is above the table.

examples.text: За поведение? Вы смеётесь надо мной?
examples.trans: For my conduct? Are you laughing at me?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'звонить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to call, to phone', paired with 'звонить'.

examples.text: Позвони мне вечером. Договоримся на завтра.
examples.trans: Call me this evening. We'll arrange something for tomorrow.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'егодня').

examples.text: Виктор Степанович, сегодня никак не могу.
examples.trans: Viktor Stepanovich, I really can't today.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'on, onto; for', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'гласить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to invite, to call in', paired with 'приглашать'.
Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to think', paired with 'подумать'.

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
